title: Improve police raid procedures: Samuel Maloney inquest jury
subtitle: London police should create better raid procedures to account for the presence of children and the mental health history of people inside a home, a coroner's inquest jury says.
article: London police should create better raid procedures to account for the presence of children and the mental health history of people inside a home, a coroner's inquest jury says.

That was one of 18 recommendations Tuesday from the five-member jury at the coroner's inquest into the death of Samuel Maloney, a London computer programmer fatally shot by city police during a raid on his Old South home on Dec. 23, 2016.

Police decided to conduct a dynamic entry - a tactical manoeuvre that involves quickly forcing their way into a location and securing it - to collect evidence and arrest Maloney as part of an investigation into the unauthorized use of the Hyland Cinema's website and email.

Maloney, 35, who had a long history of mental health struggles and clashes with authorities, was shot after he fired a crossbow at an officer and charged at others with a hatchet with his wife and two young children nearby.
The inquest, which began Jan. 14, heard from nearly a dozen witnesses, including several officers involved in the pre-dawn raid, and Maloney's common-law wife Melissa Facciolo.

"This inquest has been an opportunity for a public examination of the facts surrounding (Maloney's) death and to learn from his death to prevent similar future deaths," presiding officer Dr. David Eden said. "Our jury, as representatives of the community, has conscientiously translated that evidence into findings of facts and has written carefully considered recommendations that we all hope can be implemented."
